finding.summary: The implementation readiness engine accepted PASS evidence for several critical requirement kinds based primarily on status/confidence. Existing strict structural validation covered scenario-validation, test-data-cleanup and live-data-import, but did not require minimum real-cloud/provider/payroll/isolation receipts for tenant-environment, source-systems, historical-replay or security-controls.
finding.impact: A trusted internal worker could record high-confidence PASS evidence that did not meet the sell-readiness programme's required evidence standard, potentially allowing READY to overstate what had actually been proven. No evidence was found that this had been used to promote the frozen customer-proof release.

repair.approach: fail-closed additive wrapper around the exact current core engine
claimBoundaries: tenant environment requires non-fixture cloud-runtime provisioning with explicit zero-human, zero-intervention, health and isolation evidence
source-system readiness requires completed zero-human discovery, verified authorisation and connected non-fixture provider receipts
fixture-only providers cannot satisfy source-system readiness
live provider status requires explicit live verification
historical payroll replay must label its evidence data class and requires an independent calculation with zero unexplained variance
security controls require cloud-runtime tenant-isolation negative tests with zero critical failures
scenario validation requires cloud-runtime execution and an explicit test-data class so synthetic edge tests are not presented as production evidence
live import requires zero-human execution and an authoritative non-fixture source receipt

requiredBeforePromotion: build the exact repair candidate image
deploy only after the combined candidate is green
